name: Bura Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Andy Warren. 2003. An unreported African sign language for the deaf among the Bura in Northeast Nigeria. 4 pp. ms.
sources.note: The only item Glottolog lists as primary data; 4 pp. so possibly slightly fuller than the Ogmios note, but still 'minimal' and very unlikely to say anything about prosody.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Victoria Nyst. 2003. "An unreported African sign language in Northeast Nigeria." Ogmios: Newsletter of the Foundation for Endangered Languages 2.10 (#22), Autumn 2003, p. 14 (section 6, Reports on Field Research).
sources.note: Nothing. A one-page field note: Blench saw two deaf men signing in Kukurpu (Oct 2003), made a short videotape; Nyst comments that 'handshapes have a lax articulation', 'the signing space used is large', GO is identical to Adamorobe SL; no phonology, prosody or stress; calls for 'a descriptive study of Bura Sign Language'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page bura1295; Wikipedia 'Bura Sign Language'; Wikidata Q4998070.
sources.note: Glottolog lists only the two subclassification refs above and no descriptive reference; Wikipedia's sole citation is the Ogmios 22 note; Wikidata has no sources. OpenAlex, Crossref and Semantic Scholar queries for "Bura Sign Language" returned no further works.

sources.citation: Nyst, Victoria. 2010. Sign languages in West Africa. In D. Brentari (ed.), Sign Languages, 405-432. Cambridge: CUP.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Regional overview; p. 406 mentions Bura SL (per Glottolog). Second-hand, would only confirm that no description exists.
